questions.question: We move ______ an incredible
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__into__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **into: **If one thing gets into another, the first thing enters the second and becomes part of it.
 
• **of: **You use of after the name of someone or something to introduce the institution or place they belong to or are connected with.
 
• **so: **You use so to refer back to something that has just been mentioned.
 
• **​for: **If something is for someone, they are intended to have it or benefit from it.
 
• The correct preposition here is ‘into’ as we move ‘into’ something. The usage of the other prepositions does not fit here. Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Perceive, think ______ reflect
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__and__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **But: **You use but to introduce something which contrasts with what you have just said, or to introduce something which adds to what you have just said.
 
• **Nor: **You use nor after a negative statement in order to indicate that the negative statement also applies to you or to someone or something else.
 
• **And: **You use and to link two or more words, groups, or clauses.
 
• **So: **You use so and so that to introduce the result of the situation you have just mentioned.
 
• The correct conjunction here is ‘and’ as it joins the two words conveying the meaning that we allow ourselves to think and reflect. The sentence does not need a condition to be stated here thus the other options do not fit here. Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Ourselves to ______ movement fully
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__understand__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The word ‘**understood**’ is a verb and is in the **past tense**. We need the verb to be in the present tense as the whole passage is in the present tense. So option 1 is incorrect.
 
• The** adjective** ‘**understandable**’ does not make any sense too.
 
• **Understandably** is an **adverb**. An adverb qualifies an adjective, verb, or another adverb. Option 3 is incorrect as well.
 
• The verb ‘**understand**’ **conveys a proper meaning **that if we understand movement completely we allow ourselves to think. Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

Rohan said, “I am going”.

options.text: Rohan had said he is gone.
Rohan said that he is gone.
Rohan said that he was going.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Rohan said that he was going.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in direct speech. It has to be converted into indirect speech.
 
• 'Said' will not change because the Reporting Verb has no object. 
 
• Comma and inverted commas will be removed. 
 
• The conjunction 'That' will be added.
 
• ** 'I' **will be changed into **'he'**, according to Rohan.
 
• **Present continuous tense **will be changed into **past continuous tense.**
 
• **Thus, the sentence becomes:*** Rohan said that he was going.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The following table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech:

 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 Direct Speech
 Indirect Speech
 
 

 Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object)
 Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)
 
 

 Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
 
 

 Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object)
 Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
 
 

 Past simple (Subject+V2+Object)
 Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
 
 

 Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Past perfect continuous (Subject +had been+V1 +ing+ Object)
 
 

 Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object)
 Present Conditional (Subject+ would+V1+object)
 
 

 Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Someone has invited me to the cruise.

options.text: Someone has sent invitation to the cruise.
I had been invited to the cruise
I have been invited to the cruise.
I was invite to the cruise by somebody.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I have been invited to the cruise.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in the active voice, hence we need to convert it into the passive voice.
 
• Find the subject (someone) and object (me) of the sentence and exchange their places. Since the doer of the action is not important in the active voice, it is neglected.
 
• The given sentence is in the present perfect tense. The passive verb form for the present perfect is: 
 
 
• Has/have + been + past participle form of the verb.
 
• So, 'has invited' changes to 'have been invited' as 'I' is followed by 'have' not 'has'.
 
 
 
• At last line up the remaining part.
 
• 
 
**Following these steps, we finally get:** *I have been invited to the cruise.*

questions.question:

• **The meaning of the given words are:** 

 
 
• **Courtly **means behaving as per norm or formal and polite.

• **Elegant: **If you describe a person or thing as elegant, you mean that they are pleasing and graceful in appearance or style.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.**

Lucrative
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__worthwhile__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Lucrative: **A lucrative activity, job, or business deal is very profitable.

 
 
• ​"The new business venture turned out to be very **lucrative**, generating millions of dollars in profits within its first year of operation."
 
 
 
• **Impoverished:** made poor or with diminished quality of life
 
 
• The villagers were **impoverished **and struggled to make ends meet.
 
 
 
• **Worthwhile: **If something is worthwhile, it is enjoyable or useful, and worth the time, money, or effort that is spent on it.
 
 
• The job offered a **worthwhile **salary and benefits package.
 
 
 
• **Useless:** If something is useless, you cannot use it.
 
 
• ​The broken machine was useless and could not be repaired.
 
 
 
• **Inconsiderable:** If you describe an amount or quality as not inconsiderable, you are emphasizing that it is, in fact, large or present to a large degree.
 
 
• The difference in price between the two products was **inconsiderable **and did not affect the purchasing decision.
 
 
 
• Thus, 'worthwhile' is the most suitable answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

India is the second most populous country ______ the seventh-largest country by area in the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__and__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **But: **You use but to introduce something which contrasts with what you have just said, or to introduce something which adds to what you have just said.
 
• **However: **You use however when you are adding a comment which is surprising or which contrasts with what has just been said
 
• **And: **You use and to link two or more words, groups, or clauses.
 
• **While: **If something happens while something else is happening, the two things are happening at the same time.
 
• Since we are linking two clauses here, 'and' is suitable to use here.

**Thus, the complete sentence becomes: ***India is the second-most populous country **and** the seventh-largest country by area in the world.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Ramesh ______ into his own trap.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__fell__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Falling **is an adjective that means declining; deteriorating
 
• **'Was fall' **is grammatically incorrect, we use **'was + V₃' **in passive voice.
 
• **To fall into the trap:** If someone falls into the **trap **of doing something, they think or behave in a way that is not wise or sensible. 
 
• **Fall down: **If an argument, organization, or person falls down on a particular point, they are weak or unsatisfactory on that point. There is no such word as 'fall down into'
 
• Thus, 'fell' is most suitable.

**Thus, the complete sentence becomes: ***Ramesh **fell** **into** his own trap.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

This year, we were visited by the director of the Austrian Culture Forum, (1)/based on Delhi and together we all wanted (2)/to initiate an art festival in South India. (3)/No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__2__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **'based in Delhi' **should be there in place of **'based on Delhi'**
 
• "Based in" implies the major operations of a business or entity is contained wholly or primarily in that city.
 
• **Example: ***She is a hardware engineer based in London.*
 
• **Thus, the correct answer is: ***This year, we were visited by the director of the Austrian Culture Forum, based in Delhi and together we all wanted to initiate an art festival in South India. *
